# Review - PR 479 @ e0cdb452cd7482695c228001409c8820001f9a6a

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: 1227872ab4b693246a51e3cf5f3e699c7ddd1fe9. Five files, +89/-11 against the merge base `165dc612a951d5e452c5e828199e20049b3e4c21`: one new formalization-only finite-conditioning bound on the consistency defect, one new projective-measurement sum lemma, one deduplication onto a declaration that already exists on main, and two docstring edits.

## Findings

- none

## Review

Scope and head. Base is `main`, so the main-relative diff is the PR's own change. The worktree `.worktrees/issue-459-conditional-consistency-defect` is at exactly the published head `e0cdb452cd7482695c228001409c8820001f9a6a`, so no divergent-head reading was needed. I read `git diff 165dc612a951 e0cdb452cd78` in full (`Combining/Lines.lean`, the new `Combining/Lines/ConditionalConsistency.lean`, `Combining/Lines/SubLinePrefix.lean`, `Combining/Points/Commutation.lean`, `Combining/Points/Consistency.lean`) plus the changed files in context, and the single new commit `e0cdb452` on top of the previously reviewed head. CI at this exact head is green: `local-ci/summary` success (233s); `build`, `blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `paper-gaps`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion` all success, `blueprint-render` and `statement-origin` skipped by their path filters.

Resolution of the prior round. The only open finding at the previous head `8269f141edd2` was review 5235161053 F1: the docstring of `sum_effect_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one_of_projective` claimed an equality ("square-summable to the identity") while the declaration concludes `∑ a, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1`. That finding offered two repairs; `e0cdb452` takes the prose one, and the docstring at `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Consistency.lean:84-85` now reads "The sum of the squares of the effects of a projective measurement is bounded above by the identity", which is exactly what the `≤ 1` conclusion says in the Loewner order and is consistent with the `le_one` in the name. Declaration, name, hypotheses and proof are byte-identical to the reviewed head, so the rest of that review's ledger carries: the diff is otherwise unchanged. F1 is resolved. Earlier rounds' duplicate-helper findings are also still resolved at this head: `Points/Commutation.lean:319` calls `applyOperatorToState_finset_sum` (`Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/Consistency.lean:119`) and the local copy is deleted; the import direction `Combining/Points/*` to `Test/MagicSquareTheorems/*` has precedent elsewhere under `Combining/` and the build is green, so no cycle.

Proof integrity. `grep` over the touched Lean files finds no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`. Both new theorems are declared auxiliaries, not paper-labelled statements: `grep` over `blueprint/` finds neither name, so no `\lean`/`\leanok` obligation arises (CONTRIBUTING section 5 item 9). No existing statement, hypothesis set, quantifier order or error parameter is altered anywhere in the diff, so there is no faithfulness drift to audit. No A1-A6 anti-pattern: no conclusion-shaped hypothesis, no `:= rfl` sleight, no zero-fallback branch, no default witness, no `*Statement` smuggle.

The new bound, checked independently. `consistencyDefect_restrict_le_div_mass` (`Combining/Lines/ConditionalConsistency.lean:36-67`) unfolds `consistencyDefect` (`Games/Consistency.lean:21-30`, the `avgOver` of the off-diagonal overlaps), names the integrand, and closes with the pre-existing `avgOver_restrict_le_div_mass` (`Games/RestrictedAverage.lean:43`) applied to the pre-existing `consistencyDefect_integrand_nonneg` (`Lines/ConsistencyPositivity.lean:122`). The mathematics is right and not vacuous: `avgOver_restrict_mul_mass` (`Games/RestrictedAverage.lean:25`) pins `Distribution.restrict` down as the genuine conditional distribution (weights divided by the retained mass), the integrand is nonnegative because the two placed effects sit on opposite expanded registers, and the conclusion is the expected `defect / retained mass`. `hpos : 0 < ∑ question ∈ dist.support.filter good, dist.weight question` is a boundary condition making the conditional distribution and the division well defined, not a proof-obligation input, and the docstring's claim that pointwise nonnegativity is derived rather than assumed is accurate.

Reuse. I grepped main for pre-existing equivalents of both new declarations. `sum_mul_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_one` (`Combining/Points/Closeness.lean:87`) is the two-measurement product form and does not subsume the single-measurement lemma; `place_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one` (`Combining/Points/PlacementSupport.lean:208`) is the placed form. The closest relative of the new conditioning bound is `consistencyDefect_nondegenerateLinePastingDist_le` (`Combining/Lines/Conditioning.lean:36`), which is the specialization to `nondegenerateLinePastingDist` including the question relabeling and the `Distribution.avgOver_map` step; the new lemma is the distribution-generic form, a different statement rather than a copy. Non-blocking note, not a finding: once this lands, that specialized lemma could be rewritten through the generic one, and neither new declaration yet has a consumer under `MIPStarRE/` - expected for a staged proof packet, and CONTRIBUTING section 5 item 7 asks only that new lemmas be reusable, which they are.

Prose. The diff's mathematical prose is Lean documentation only (no blueprint TeX, paper-gap or audit file is touched), so I reviewed it under the prose lane's equivalence-and-status rules. The new module docstring and both declaration docstrings state exactly what is proved and label the conditioning bound a formalization-only auxiliary. I verified both added locators against the in-repo mirror: `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:936-963` is the `eq:pasting-q1` conditioning step feeding `lem:pasting`, which is the argument the estimate supports; and the `SubLinePrefix.lean:22-23` addition is correct, since `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-237` is precisely `eq:cl-dlnf` and the accompanying explanation that `π_{i-1}` zeroes the first `i-1` coordinates, i.e. the prefix restriction the module describes.

Style. Module docstring with `## References` present on the new file; lengths 71 / 417 / 449 lines are inside the limit and `local-ci/file-length` is green; names are paper-facing and Mathlib-cased; the new module is wired into the `Combining/Lines.lean` umbrella. Both touched proof files elaborate clean in the PR worktree: `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/ConditionalConsistency.lean` and `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Consistency.lean` each returned rc=0 with no output.

Not checked. I did not run a bare `lake build` (the machine-wide build lock belongs to the gate; I relied on the green `local-ci/build` at this head), did not run `#print axioms` on the new declarations, and did not re-derive the paper's conditioning step line by line - the locator is a "supporting" reference for a formalization-only finite-probability estimate, matching the locator `Games/RestrictedAverage.lean:11-12` already carries on main. I also did not review the merge commits' inherited content, which is main.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=APPROVED)
